residencyRequirements.description: Washington has no minimum residency period prior to filing. However, at least one party must be a resident of Washington at the time of filing with the intent to remain. The action is filed in the county where either party resides.

waitingPeriod.description: Washington requires a mandatory 90-day waiting period from the date the petition is filed AND service on the respondent (or respondent's first appearance) must have occurred before a decree can be entered. Both conditions must be satisfied. (RCW 26.09.030)

groundsForDissolution.notes: Washington is a pure no-fault state. The only ground for dissolution of marriage is that the marriage is irretrievably broken. Fault or misconduct is not relevant to the dissolution.

propertyDivision.description: Washington is a community property state. All property acquired during the marriage is presumed to be community property. The court shall make a just and equitable disposition of the property and liabilities, considering all relevant factors. In practice, courts generally divide community property equally.

parentingPlan.description: Washington requires the parties to submit a proposed Parenting Plan. The court enters a final Parenting Plan that includes a Residential Schedule specifying where the children will reside, and a decision-making allocation.

filingFees.notes: Washington's dissolution filing fee varies by county (e.g., approximately $314 in Pierce County, $364 in some other counties). A fee waiver may be available for low-income petitioners whose household income is at or below 125% of the federal poverty guidelines.

childSupportGuidelines.description: Washington uses the Washington State Child Support Schedule, an income shares model based on an economic table. Both parents' combined monthly net incomes are matched to the economic table to determine the basic support obligation. The obligation is then apportioned based on each parent's share of combined net income. Adjustments apply for health insurance, daycare, special child-rearing expenses, and the residential schedule.
childSupportGuidelines.statute: RCW 26.19; Washington State Child Support Schedule
childSupportGuidelines.notes: Effective January 1, 2026 (EHB 1014): The economic table is expanded to cover combined monthly net incomes up to $50,000 (previously capped at $12,000). The self-support reserve is increased from 125% to 180% of the federal poverty guideline for a one-person family. The low-income floor is raised from $1,000 to $2,200 combined monthly income. Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) and WA Cares premiums are now deductible from gross income. These changes apply to all new and modified orders entered on or after January 1, 2026.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Washington has no statutory formula for spousal maintenance. The court considers the financial resources of the maintenance-seeking party, the time necessary to acquire education or training, the standard of living during the marriage, the duration of the marriage, the age, physical and emotional condition, and financial obligations of the spouse seeking maintenance, and the ability of the supporting spouse to meet their own needs while paying maintenance.
factors: Financial resources of the party seeking maintenance
Time necessary to acquire education or training for appropriate employment
Standard of living established during the marriage
Age, physical and emotional condition, and financial obligations of the spouse seeking maintenance
Ability of the spouse from whom maintenance is sought to meet own needs while paying maintenance

court.name: Superior Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the Superior Court of the county where either party resides.
